name: Sandisk Corporation
research_rationale: On-file FCF and earnings stay exceptional and the Nvidia-led memory bounce helps, but 2027 NAND oversupply press, post-split volatility and a proposed officer sale keep research weakening the strong-buy screen.

weekly_updates.summary:
GF Securities’s 2027 NAND glut warning dragged Sandisk with Micron; press frames it as the most NAND-exposed name.
Duquesne’s 13F showed a full exit before 30 September; the 8-for-1 split is scheduled for 19 November.
Memory names remain volatile on AI-demand fears; bullish NAND notes (e.g. Evercore) sit alongside sharp recent share losses.

Press contrasts brisk AI data-centre NAND sales with falling shares and political/regulatory fears hitting memory stocks.
After-hours chip names firmed on Nvidia’s earnings beat; the batch adds no new SNDK filings or company disclosures.

Headlines tie a further slide to NAND oversupply fears and the 19 November 8-for-1 split; SNDK is framed as the most exposed memory name.
ETF flow pieces report net selling (~$41m on 16 Nov; iShares AI Innovation cut ~$64m); Zacks downgrade sits beside split-week bull notes.
No new company filings in the batch; Nvidia-led sector firming offers only indirect support.

Press reports another ~3.3% share fall on 18 November, still framed around NAND cycle anxiety ahead of the 19 November split.
Commentary favours SK Hynix over Micron and Sandisk for 2027; the batch adds no new SNDK filings or company disclosures.

Split-week press links Micron split speculation to Sandisk’s announced 8-for-1 split on 19 November; no issuer filing in the batch.  
One bullish 2027 price piece argues the recent slide is overdone; NAND cyclical anxiety still dominates peer commentary.  
Refreshed financials in file still show strong FCF and revenue; no new SNDK disclosures.

On 19 November, split-day headlines and a ~4% memory bounce (Anthropic IPO-led AI trade) sit with pieces calling Sandisk cheap versus Micron; the 8-for-1 split lands today.
GF Securities’s 2027 NAND glut narrative and mixed 13F flows (Ken Fisher among buyers; Duquesne full exit) still frame cycle anxiety.
No new SNDK issuer filings in the batch; on-file financials still show very strong cash flow.

Post-split trading drew 14–16% falls and worst-week-since-July framing tied to TrendForce’s bearish 2027 NAND view and Morningstar bust commentary; the 8-for-1 split is now in effect.  
On 23 November, Jensen Huang’s return at Nvidia lifted AI/memory names (~12% SNDK); Citi argues the Micron–Sandisk slide is overdone, beside value-trap versus “numbers still ridiculous” debate.  
No new SNDK issuer filings in the batch; refreshed on-file financials still show very strong free cash flow.

Nvidia-led chip rally kept SNDK in headline flow with a sharp Micron rebound; press still debates post-split bargain versus full valuation.
The batch cites a proposed officer share sale (~$2.37M); no new issuer filings in the pack.
Refreshed on-file financials still show very strong free cash flow.
